study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of molecular-based functional circuits captures clinical heterogeneity transdiagnostically in psychiatric patients

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: CamCAN (Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience) dataset was used for healthy ageing spanning the full spectrum of healthy ageing. UCLA phenomics dataset (part of Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics - CNP) was used for healthy individuals and multiple psychiatric cohorts (SCHZ, BPD, ADHD) with deep clinical phenotyping.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: This study utilises two separate existing datasets. Firstly, the healthy ageing CamCAN dataset (obtained from the CamCAN repository available at http://www.mrc-cbu.cam.ac.uk/datasets/CamCAN/) was chosen as it spans the full spectrum of healthy ageing... Secondly, the UCLA phenomics dataset (ref. 120, available from https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds000030/versions/1.0.0), was selected as it included healthy individuals as well as multiple psychiatric cohorts with deep clinical phenotyping

answer.Cam-CAN: Normative model training (70%) and testing (30%) for healthy controls

answer.CNP: Normative model training (70%) and testing (30%) for healthy controls; Clinical cohorts (SCHZ, BPD, ADHD) for deviation analysis and transdiagnostic symptom mapping

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Both CamCAN and UCLA healthy control data were used to train normative models (70/30 train-test split: CamCAN=346/150, UCLA=78/33). The UCLA dataset also provided three clinical cohorts (SCHZ N=38, BPD N=44, ADHD N=37) used to examine deviations from normality within and across conventional diagnostic boundaries.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: A set of HBR models were trained on healthy participants data from both the UCLA and CamCAN datasets, utilising a 70/30 train test split... resulting in CamCAN = 346/150 and UCLA = 78/33 train/test subdivisions... Predictions using these models were also made for the clinical cohorts, where age and sex were used to predict their molecular-enriched networks.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) normative model was built for molecular-enriched functional connectivity. Total 607 healthy subjects from combined CamCAN (N=496) and UCLA (N=111) datasets. Training phase used 70% of data: CamCAN=346, UCLA=78 (total=424). Testing phase used 30% of data: CamCAN=150, UCLA=33 (total=183).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: Following quality control exclusions, imaging data of a total of 607 healthy subjects (CamCAN: N=496, Mean age (SD) = 52.3 (18.3), M/F = 255/241; UCLA: N=111, Mean age (SD) = 31.2 (8.7), M/F = 60/51) were included in the analysis... A set of HBR models were trained on healthy participants data from both the UCLA and CamCAN datasets, utilising a 70/30 train test split... resulting in CamCAN = 346/150 and UCLA = 78/33 train/test subdivisions.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: CamCAN (N=496): Mean=52.3, SD=18.3; UCLA HC (N=111): Mean=31.2, SD=8.7. Weighted mean for overall (N=607): (496*52.3 + 111*31.2)/607 = 48.44 years. Pooled SD: sqrt(((495*18.3^2 + 110*8.7^2)/605)) = 16.96. Train phase estimates assume similar distribution in 70% split. CamCAN spans full healthy ageing spectrum; UCLA has younger adult sample. Min/max not reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: Following quality control exclusions, imaging data of a total of 607 healthy subjects (CamCAN: N=496, Mean age (SD) = 52.3 (18.3), M/F = 255/241; UCLA: N=111, Mean age (SD) = 31.2 (8.7), M/F = 60/51) were included in the analysis.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Overall phase (N=607): CamCAN M/F=255/241 + UCLA M/F=60/51 = Total M=315 (51.9%), F=292 (48.1%). Train phase (N=424) was estimated by applying 70% ratio to each dataset: CamCAN (346): ~179M/167F; UCLA (78): ~42M/36F; Total ~221M/203F. This is an approximation as the exact train split by sex is not reported.
